description:
<!-- Modified by lavinhoque33, 2026-11-11. -->
## Features and fixes

### YouTube

- **Sync with anddea/revanced-patches:** Includes the changes through v4.4.0-dev.6.
- **Glass navigation bar spacing:** A bottom spacing slider in the size dialog sets how far the capsule floats above the screen edge. Snackbars appear just above the navigation bar.
- **Navigation bar:** Translucent, Transparent and Glass styles no longer leave an empty black or white strip below the feed. Buttons no longer sit too high with gesture navigation, including with Glass off. The capsule follows Morphe's placement. Blur is used only on Android 14 and newer; Android 12 and 13 keep a plain translucent fill to avoid crashes while the player moves.
- **Feed cards:** Fix density-dependent margins, black thumbnail gutters, square corners, undersized cards and disrupted layouts around inline previews. Grid cards stay within their columns, and dynamic colors tint the whole card below the thumbnail. Playlists, mixes and podcasts follow the Classic layout or card background like videos, including while templates update.
- **Unlock queue:** With Unlock queue on, Play next in queue in the feed menu uses YouTube's own queue. Add to RVX queue still opens the RVX queue dialog. Turn Unlock queue off to override the feed queue button. Premium-style queue takes priority when enabled.
- **Native About screen:** About stays last in RVX settings and is excluded from search. App info, Actions and More contain eight themed icon rows, with app and patch versions and patch time as summaries. GitHub, report, feature request, credits and Copy debug info actions remain available, and custom settings branding is preserved.
- **Playlist download picker:** Rounded Select all, Select none and Edit buttons use sentence-case, wrapping labels. Download spans the width. Options and video rows scroll independently, while selection controls and Download stay available in portrait and landscape. The single-video picker is unchanged.
- **Download option icons:** Show download option icons, off by default, adds icons beside Include subtitles and Include SponsorBlock in the built-in downloader.
- **Feature flags manager:** RVX settings > Miscellaneous > Debugging includes a Feature flags manager with Binary search to help find problematic flags. If flag overrides or a search cause two failed starts, the third start resets them and explains what happened.
- **Toolbar:** The Create button opens the upload menu again.
- **Watch later improvements:** Options widen Watch later drag handles and hide the snackbar after removing a video.
- **Post buttons:** Hide post like, share and comment buttons, or give posts the same grouped button layout.
- **Captions:** Stable caption blocks and two languages at once on YouTube 21.15 and newer.
- **Spoof video streams:** Fetch streams sooner for faster starts and keep inline feed previews muted.

### YouTube Music

- **Track crossfade:** Keep the incoming track silent until its fade begins, preserve its volume normalization, and avoid applying fade gain twice. Keep outgoing audio effects attached until playback finishes, with improved player/session cleanup. Crossfade is no longer incorrectly disabled merely because stream spoofing is off; local stream-copy playback remains eligible. Versions below 9.00 retain the existing warning and skip this patch.
- **Lyrics:** Dynamic lyrics backgrounds and furigana, showing each Japanese word's reading above the text.
- **One Download method:** Miscellaneous > Downloads now has one method for individual songs, playlists and albums: Stream download (default), Device files, or YouTube Music / external app. Stream download keeps private copies for playback online and offline. Device files saves to the device library. External overrides apply to individual songs; playlists and albums stay with Music. A download never writes both kinds of copy. Earlier choices migrate to Stream first, then Device files, without deleting existing downloads.
- **Download quality:** One quality setting covers future individual, playlist and album downloads: Highest (default), High, Normal or Low. It applies to Stream download and Device files, is captured once per download or batch, and is disabled for YouTube Music / external app. Existing copies are not redownloaded or transcoded.
- **Source quality tiers:** Highest prefers the best available source, including AAC 141 or Opus 774 around 256 kbps when offered. High prefers Opus 251; Normal prefers AAC 140 around 128 kbps; Low prefers HE-AAC 139 around 48 kbps or Opus 249 around 50 kbps. Missing tiers fall back to available sources. Source tiers, not variable-bitrate file sizes, determine quality. This does not unlock Premium formats or manufacture higher quality by transcoding.
- **Individual stream downloads:** Download a song from its menu or player, even when the account has no stock Download menu item. Individual downloads save audio, including from Video mode or an album row showing the music video. Failures name the reason.
- **Local playback, online features:** Saved copies play locally while radio, lyrics and the queue remain online whenever connected. They also play fully offline, including with Spoof video streams enabled. Each copy retains its original codec and stream identity. Stream downloads shows their size and can remove them without touching device files.
- **Green checks:** A green check at the right end of a song row indicates a stream copy, not a device-file download. Checks appear on playlists, album tracks, the Search songs filter and player queue, including individually saved songs on albums that were never downloaded. A fully downloaded playlist or album also marks its header Download button. Checks are on by default.
- **Audio first:** Downloaded songs start in Song mode by default, including from album rows, Play and Next. For songs without a saved video, the switch can still reach the online video and retain position in both directions, unless position is unknown or within three seconds of the end.
- **Saved video:** Album downloads save a matched 360p music video when available, paired with audio at the selected quality. Matching uses title or similar duration; uncertain matches save no video. Playlists without server-linked music videos save audio only, and individual downloads save no video. A video failure does not fail the song or list. Completion messages and Stream downloads include videos and their size; removing stream copies removes their videos too.
- **Instant Song/Video switch:** A song with a saved video uses the saved picture/audio pair in both modes, online and offline. Music's native switch flips in place without reloading, interrupting audio or changing position. Song mode uses the pair's audio track. Track taps start the selected song, and Next and song-end continuation keep the chosen mode. Offline seeking works in Video mode too.
- **Offline player:** Keep song details and album covers for offline playback; earlier copies fill in details while online. Open downloaded songs reports how many are offline ready. The No connection sheet no longer covers playback controls. Offline album taps play the selected track, not the first track. Play one saved video online after installing this version to retain the settings needed for offline video.
- **Downloads inside the Library:** Downloads is a chip filter, with Songs, Playlists and Albums filters, not a separate Library page. Individually downloaded songs are grouped into No Playlist. Downloads refreshes rows and counts after downloads, removals and Back navigation. After restart the Library tab opens the Library, not Downloads, with working back navigation. Device files uses Music's native device-files library without deleting stream copies.
- **No Playlist:** Loose saved songs open in a full-screen list with right-side checks and play in shown order from the song tapped, online and offline. Online, rows preceding the tapped song follow the end of the list before radio; playback uses local audio while retaining lyrics and radio.
- **Full song menus:** Three-dot and long-press actions on a No Playlist song open Music's native menu for that exact song, with available Share, album, playlist, queue and other stock actions. Opening another song's menu does not change playback or queue. Complete menus are saved for offline use; earlier copies need No Playlist opened online once to obtain them.
- **Remove download:** A saved song's Download action, including in the player menu, becomes Remove download with confirmation. A fully saved playlist or album offers the same action. Copies still needed by another downloaded list or individual download are retained. Download actions are not duplicated alongside Music's newer menu rows.
- **Interrupted or unavailable tracks:** Interrupted lists no longer leave tracks in No Playlist or count as complete. Download finishes the job; checks and Remove download appear when all available tracks are saved. Deleted, private or blocked tracks do not fail the whole download; completion reports skipped tracks.
- **Native offline pages:** Open a downloaded playlist or album online to record its native page, about 90 KB per playlist or 22 KB per album. It then opens offline with header, cover, rows and checks, including from the Albums chip. Tapping a track plays its local copy and continues through the list. Online, Downloads rows open the normal online page, never a redownload prompt; connection state is checked when tapped.
- **Android Auto:** Downloaded Playlists includes stream copies and No Playlist with artwork, independently of Device files. Starting a saved track no longer crashes or stalls after an online session. Playback uses local audio and retains online features while connected, and also works after a fully offline cold start. No Playlist inserts following songs together in order before radio. Next, Previous, rapid selections and reconnects cannot let an older request replace the current queue; menu lookups do not change it. Explicit Video selection may still stream the online video.

## Compatibility and verification

Supported patching versions:
- YouTube: **21.39.525, 21.13.164, 20.05.46**.
- YouTube Music: **9.40.51, 9.15.51, 8.30.54**.

Runtime checks used the rooted Moto Edge Plus 2023 with YouTube 21.39.525 and Music 9.40.51. Music checks covered local playback online and offline, AAC after an online session and from a fully offline cold start, seeking, saved video/audio pairs, and native No Playlist menus without disturbing another song's queue. Android Auto was exercised through the Desktop Head Unit, including artwork, ordered Next/Previous, radio after saved lists, rapid selections, reconnection and offline cold starts; its real Next button advanced from saved AAC 140 to saved Opus 251.

The final crossfade changes were exercised with the original spoof-off settings and local FILE playback: natural fade, chained manual skip and pause-abort/resume. Logs showed initial silence, an equal-power ramp and outgoing release. This does not prove that the reported Poco/HyperOS audible burst is fixed. Native About actions, search exclusion and icon variants passed. The final playlist picker passed portrait and landscape checks with 25 entries, independent scrolling, selection and per-row Edit; no download was queued during this UI check.

On the test account, High saved Opus 251, Normal AAC 140 (128,331 bps), Low HE-AAC 139 (48,492 bps), and Highest saved Opus 251 because 141/774 were not offered. The saved 360p test pair used video 134 and AAC 140. Live Premium 141/774 availability, measured normalization gain, external equalizer attachment and PCM measurement of zero audible interruption were not verified.

Also not verified at runtime: the four older supported app versions; navigation fixes on Android 15+, HyperOS gestures or Opaque style; completed Feature flags Binary search (unit-tested only); light theme for the final changes; large fonts or narrow split-screen layouts; YouTube offline-library serving after the spoof change; affected-account feed cards; server-linked playlist music videos; song-end auto-advance or offline Previous in Video mode; an offline-restored player; or a physical car head unit. Literal Music 6.2.0 was not exercised; the existing below-9.00 crossfade skip was checked on 6.20.51.

Known behavior:
- A native playlist or album page is recorded only when opened online. Until then, offline playback starts from its first downloaded song.
- Covers never seen online can appear as grey squares offline; only Music's image cache is used.
- A Downloads view drawn online and tapped immediately after losing network can show a spinner for about six seconds before opening.
- Earlier individual copies need No Playlist opened online once to retain their complete native menus offline.
- The builder's existing YouTube light-theme background option is ignored because Theme has no `lightThemeBackgroundColor` option. Both CLI versions used in previous release checks warned about it without failing patching.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/lavinhoque33/revanced-patches/compare/v1.33.0...v1.34.0)
